The core mathematical structure revolves around time-series analysis of player movements and binary decision trees. The pocket release time (2.80s) acts as a critical threshold; if the defense can collapse the pocket faster, the quarterback faces a forced throw or sack. This ties into the Run Yield Over Expectation (RYOE) metric, which measures the efficiency of running plays. When combined with the defensive front's activation status, we create a unified framework that predicts whether the offensive line will hold up against the pass rush or if the running game will break down due to poor leverage. The "breaking condition" introduces a stochastic element—player injuries and blitz adjustments—that disrupts the deterministic model, requiring Bayesian updating of expectations.
